correctness.rationale: The proof excludes nonleaf layers using unique tree-centered length-two paths; proves necessity of independent feasible restrictions by convexity; and explicitly constructs shortest paths through a nonleaf layer for all cross-layer endpoints, proving a literal simplicial join. For the rook prism, each distance-two pair has exactly the two opposite corners as possible middle vertices, so the forbidden cross-row pair criterion yields exactly two row simplices with n bridge edges. Exact face/facet counts and a simplicial collapse to a connected graph with cycle rank n-1 prove the integral circle wedge; joining ell copies gives the stated sphere wedge. The standalone verifier exhaustively checks 12800 leaf-support masks across five finite graphs and mod-two homology for three; finite checks are only corroboration.

value.rationale: The full feasible-set factorization is a natural structural analogue of a well-studied product invariant, allowing exact distributions of all feasible and inclusion-maximal sets for any tree leaf number. The rook-prism case gives an all-parameter family of complexes with integral homology rank (n-1)^ell in degree 2ell-1, explicit nonpure facet spectra and a purity phase n=2; none of this follows from the previously known maximum-cardinality equality alone. The invariant is canonical, not an arbitrary finite slice.
